chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad from Salih ibn Abi Hammad said:

I asked the Knowledgeable One (peace be upon him) about sneezing and what is the reason for saying 'Praise be to Allah' upon it. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'For Allah has a favor upon His servant regarding the health of his body and the safety of his limbs, and the servant tends to forget the Mention of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, upon that; and when he forgets, Allah commands the wind, so it passes through his body, then He expels it from his nose, so he praises Allah upon that, and that praise of his at that time becomes a thankfulness for what he had forgotten.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reason for saying Alhamdulillah when sneezing in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), linking the physical act of sneezing to a divine mechanism where wind expels impurities, serving as a subtle reminder for the distracted believer. The Imam elucidates that the subsequent 'Alhamdulillah' is not merely a reaction to the sneeze, but a compensatory gratitude for the remembrance of Allah that was momentarily overlooked during the bodily process. This highlights the Shia scholarly view of mundane bodily functions as opportunities for spiritual mindfulness and thanksgiving.
